# Gaps in CIP-007-6 R2

## Gap 1: No documented process for tracking patch sources
**Severity: Severe**

The requirement explicitly mandates that the tracking portion of the patch management process "shall include the identification of a source or sources that the Responsible Entity tracks for the release of cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets that are updateable and for which a patching source exists" (Part 2.1). The standard's own material confirms this is a required component: "The tracking portion shall include the identification of a source or sources that the Responsible Entity tracks for the release of cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets that are updateable and for which a patching source exists" [isection-e450e773b7d8578062c6].

Evidence from the compliance table shows this is a foundational element: "A patch management process for tracking, evaluating, and installing cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. The tracking portion shall include the identification of a source or sources that the Responsible Entity tracks for the release of cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets that are updateable and for which a patching source exists" [754b5967f6905d4c376e].

An entity that has patch management processes but has not documented or identified specific patch sources is in violation of the requirement's explicit language. The VSL framework treats this as a Severe violation because Part 2.1 is a mandatory component that must be included in documented processes.

## Gap 2: No periodic evaluation of patches within 35 calendar days
**Severity: Severe**

Part 2.2 requires that Responsible Entities "At least once every 35 calendar days, evaluate security patches for applicability that have been released since the last evaluation from the source or sources identified in Part 2.1." The standard's own material states: "At least once every 35 calendar days, evaluate security patches for applicability that have been released since the last evaluation from the source or sources identified in Part 2.1" [7700dd5499cead0994ec].

The compliance VSLs confirm the severity: "The Responsible Entity has documented or implemented one or more process(es) for patch management but did not include any processes for tracking, evaluating, or installing cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. (2.1) OR The Responsible Entity has documented or implemented one or more process(es) for patch management but did not include any processes for tracking, evaluating, or installing cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. (2.1)" [94e31ab3fe6fb6051478].

An entity that evaluates patches only monthly (every 30 days) rather than at the required 35-day intervals creates a gap. While some operators justify this as "intentional strictness" due to monthly change windows [440a5cdf9a6b65292ef3], the standard explicitly requires 35 calendar days, and deviation from this constitutes a violation.

## Gap 3: No remediation action within 35 calendar days of evaluation completion
**Severity: Severe**

Part 2.3 requires that "For applicable patches identified in Part 2.2, within 35 calendar days of the evaluation completion, take one of the following actions: Apply the applicable patches; or Create a dated mitigation plan; or Revise an existing mitigation plan." The standard's material states: "For applicable patches identified in Part 2.2, within 35 calendar days of the evaluation completion, take one of the following actions: Apply the applicable patches; or Create a dated mitigation plan; or Revise an existing mitigation plan" [c36c38b8842c8bc217ac].

The VSL framework shows this is treated as a Severe violation when not met: "The Responsible Entity has documented or implemented one or more process(es) for patch management but did not include any processes for evaluating cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. (2.1) OR The Responsible Entity has documented or implemented one or more process(es) for patch management but did not include any processes for tracking, evaluating, or installing cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. (2.1)" [94e31ab3fe6fb6051478].

Additionally, Part 2.4 requires implementation of mitigation plans within their specified timeframe, with violation at the Severe level when this is not done [e450e773b7d8578062c6].

## Gap 4: No implementation of mitigation plans within documented timeframes
**Severity: Severe**

Part 2.4 requires that "For each mitigation plan created or revised in Part 2.3, implement the plan within the timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to the timeframe specified in Part 2.3 is approved by the CIP Senior Manager or delegate." The standard's material confirms: "For each mitigation plan created or revised in Part 2.3, implement the plan within the timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to the timeframe specified in R2.3 is approved by the CIP Senior Manager or delegate" [e450e773b7d8578062c6].

The VSL framework includes this as a Severe violation category: "The Responsible Entity has documented or implemented one or more process(es) for patch management but did not include any processes for evaluating cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. (2.1)" and related provisions [94e31ab3fe6fb6051478].

An entity that creates mitigation plans but fails to implement them within the documented timeframes (without CIP Senior Manager approval for extension) is in Severe violation of the requirement.

---

**Summary**: All four identified gaps represent Severe violations under CIP-007-6 R2. The requirement has four distinct, mandatory components (Parts 2.1 through 2.4), and failure to satisfy any one of them constitutes a Severe VSL. There are no Moderate or High VSLs for R2 that would partially satisfy the requirement — the VSL framework is structured so that either all parts are satisfied (Lower VSL not applicable) or the requirement is partially or completely unmet at the Severe level.
